```{r setup-and-import, message=FALSE}

# --- Load ALL necessary libraries ---
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
library(DESeq2)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(indicspecies)
library(FSA) # For Dunn's Test
library(tidyverse) # For data manipulation

# --- Read OTU Table ---
otu_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.subsample.shared", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")


otu_mat <- otu_raw[, -(1:3)]


rownames(otu_mat) <- otu_raw$Group 


otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)


otu_tab <- otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)


# --- Read and Process Taxonomy ---
tax_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.cons.taxonomy", sep = "\t", header = TRUE, quote = "")
taxonomy_clean <- lapply(strsplit(tax_raw$Taxonomy, ";"), function(x) {
    x <- gsub("\\(.*?\\)|\\\"", "", x[nchar(x) > 0]); trimws(x)
})
max_ranks <- 7; taxonomy_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(taxonomy_clean, `length<-`, max_ranks))
colnames(taxonomy_mat) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
rownames(taxonomy_mat) <- tax_raw$OTU
tax_tab <- tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy_mat))
```

```{r phyloseq-object}

# Read OTU table
otu_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.subsample.shared", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")

# Set rownames of the matrix (Taxa) before transposing
# The original row names are NOT needed as they are just row numbers.

# Extract only the count data columns (from column 4 onwards)
otu_mat <- otu_raw[, -(1:3)]

# CRITICAL: Set the row names of the matrix (these are the sample IDs)
# This MUST be done before transposing
rownames(otu_mat) <- otu_raw$Group 

# Transpose the matrix so OTUs are rows and Samples are columns
# Now, otu_mat has OTUs as rows (OTU IDs) and Samples as columns (Sample IDs)
otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)

# Create phyloseq OTU table
# taxa_are_rows = TRUE is correct after the transpose
otu_tab <- otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)

# Check the result
head(otu_tab)



```

```{r}
# --- 1. Read the taxonomy file ---
tax_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.cons.taxonomy", 
                      sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, quote = "")

# --- 2. Extract taxonomy strings and OTU IDs ---
taxonomy_strings <- tax_raw$Taxonomy
names(taxonomy_strings) <- tax_raw$OTU

# --- 3. Split taxonomy strings by ';' and clean ---
taxonomy_clean <- strsplit(taxonomy_strings, ";")

taxonomy_clean <- lapply(taxonomy_clean, function(x) {
  x <- x[nchar(x) > 0]                # Remove empty strings
  x <- gsub("\\(.*?\\)", "", x)       # Remove confidence scores in parentheses
  x <- gsub('\\"', '', x)              # Remove escaped quotes
  trimws(x)                           # Trim whitespace
})

# --- 4. Pad each taxonomy vector to length 7 (Kingdom to Species) ---
max_ranks <- 7
taxonomy_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(taxonomy_clean, function(x) {
  length(x) <- max_ranks  # pad with NAs if needed
  x
}))

# --- 5. Assign column and row names ---
colnames(taxonomy_mat) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
rownames(taxonomy_mat) <- names(taxonomy_strings)

# --- 6. Create tax_table object for phyloseq ---
tax_tab <- tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy_mat))

# --- Optional: Check the result ---
head(tax_tab)
```



```{r phyloseq-object-final}

# Make sure the sample names really match
otu_names  <- sample_names(otu_tab)
meta_names <- rownames(Kohler.design)

length(otu_names); length(meta_names)
intersect(otu_names, meta_names)

# Keep shared samples only
common_samples <- intersect(otu_names, meta_names)
length(common_samples)   # Should be > 0!

# Prune OTU table
otu_tab_pruned <- prune_samples(common_samples, otu_tab)

# Create sample_data object
sample_data_obj <- sample_data(Kohler.design[common_samples, ])

# Build phyloseq object
physeq <- phyloseq(otu_tab_pruned, tax_tab, sample_data_obj)

physeq
```


```{r data-prep-alpha-data}
# 1. Filter and Rarefy (Creates physeq_rarefied)
physeq_filt <- filter_taxa(physeq, function(x) sum(x > 3) > (0.2 * length(x)), TRUE)
min_depth <- min(sample_sums(physeq_filt)); set.seed(42)
physeq_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(physeq_filt, sample.size = min_depth, replace = FALSE)

# 2. Calculate Diversity (Creates alpha_diversity_rarefied)
alpha_diversity_rarefied <- estimate_richness(physeq_rarefied, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon"))

# 3. Merge Diversity and Metadata (Creates alpha_data_rarefied)
sample_metadata_rarefied <- as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq_rarefied))
alpha_data_rarefied <- cbind(alpha_diversity_rarefied, sample_metadata_rarefied) 

# 4. Order Factors (Crucial for correct plotting order)
age_order <- c("Fetus", "Newborn", "7+days", "15+days", "20+days")
alpha_data_rarefied$Age <- factor(alpha_data_rarefied$Age, levels = age_order)

treat <- c("Muck", "Sterile")
alpha_data_rarefied$SampleType <- factor(alpha_data_rarefied$SampleType, levels= treat)

mother <- c("11.21","11.22","NR-1910","NR1908","NR1910","NR1912","RNR1912")
alpha_data_rarefied$Mother <- factor(alpha_data_rarefied$Mother, levels= mother)

```

```{r alpha-diversity-plot}
# Plot Alpha Diversity
ggplot(alpha_data_rarefied, aes(x = Age, y = Shannon)) +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(title = "Alpha Diversity (Shannon Index) by Age and Sample Type", x = "Age", y = "Shannon Diversity Index") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1️⃣ Split the alpha-diversity data by SampleType ---
alpha_muck    <- alpha_data_rarefied %>% filter(SampleType == "Muck")
alpha_sterile <- alpha_data_rarefied %>% filter(SampleType == "Sterile")


# --- 2️⃣ Inspect the two filtered tables ---
cat("Muck samples:\n")
print(alpha_muck)

cat("\nSterile samples:\n")
print(alpha_sterile)

# --- 3️⃣ Plot Shannon diversity by Age for each SampleType separately ---

p_muck <- ggplot(alpha_muck, aes(x = Age, y = Shannon, color = Age)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, fill = "lightgreen", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Shannon Diversity by Age (Muck Samples)",
       x = "Age", y = "Shannon Diversity Index") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p_sterile <- ggplot(alpha_sterile, aes(x = Age, y = Shannon, color = Age)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Shannon Diversity by Age (Sterile Samples)",
       x = "Age", y = "Shannon Diversity Index") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# --- 4️⃣ Display both plots ---
print(p_muck)
print(p_sterile)
```
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# 1️⃣  Exclude Fetus & Newborn
alpha_plotdata <- alpha_data_rarefied %>%
  filter(!Age %in% c("Fetus", "Newborn"))

# 2️⃣  Define order for remaining ages
age_order <- c("7+days", "15+days", "20+days")
alpha_plotdata$Age <- factor(alpha_plotdata$Age, levels = age_order)

# 3️⃣  Convert data from wide to long for easy faceting
alpha_long <- alpha_plotdata %>%
  select(SampleType, Age, Observed, Shannon) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Observed", "Shannon"),
               names_to = "Metric",
               values_to = "Value")

# 4️⃣  Side‑by‑side boxplots with points, faceted by Metric
ggplot(alpha_long, aes(x = Age, y = Value, fill = SampleType)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
               width = 0.7, alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, color = "gray30") +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = SampleType),
              position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8),
              size = 2, alpha = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ Metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Alpha Diversity by Age (Fetus & Newborn excluded)",
       x = "Age",
       y = "Diversity value",
       fill = "Sample Type",
       color = "Sample Type") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray95"))
```

```{r beta-diversi}
# Load necessary packages
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
library(dplyr)

# Calculate distance matrix (Bray–Curtis)
dist_matrix <- phyloseq::distance(physeq, method = "bray")

# Perform NMDS ordination (with higher trymax for stability)
set.seed(123)
ord <- ordinate(physeq, method = "NMDS", distance = dist_matrix, trymax = 100)

# Extract sample data for plotting
sample_data_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq))

# Plot NMDS ordination with ellipses, stress label, and sample names
p <- plot_ordination(physeq, ord, color = "SampleType") +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", linetype = 2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = rownames(sample_data_df)), size = 3, vjust = -0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 2,
           label = paste("Stress =", round(ord$stress, 3)),
           size = 4, color = "black") +
  labs(title = "NMDS Ordination (Bray–Curtis)",
       color = "Sample Type") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

# Display the plot
p
```

```{r permanova}
library(vegan)

# 1️⃣ Coerce your metadata into a *plain data.frame* (no extra classes)
Kohler.design <- data.frame(sample_data(physeq))

# 2️⃣ Ensure factor variables are properly recognized
# (Optional, but it helps)
Kohler.design$SampleType <- as.factor(Kohler.design$SampleType)
Kohler.design$Age <- as.factor(Kohler.design$Age)
Kohler.design$Mother <- as_factor(Kohler.design$Mother)
Kohler.design$Feed <- as.factor(Kohler.design$Feed)

# 3️⃣ Match metadata order to the distance matrix order
Kohler.design <- Kohler.design[match(rownames(as.matrix(dist_matrix)),
                                     rownames(Kohler.design)), , drop = FALSE]

# 4️⃣ Confirm the rownames really match
stopifnot(all(rownames(as.matrix(dist_matrix)) == rownames(Kohler.design)))

# 5️⃣ Run the PERMANOVA correctly
set.seed(42)
permanova_res <- adonis2(as.matrix(dist_matrix) ~ SampleType + Age + Mother + Feed,
                         data = Kohler.design,
                         permutations = 999)

# 6️⃣ View the output
print(permanova_res)
```

```{r permanova-final}
adonis2(as.matrix(dist_matrix) ~ SampleType + Age + Feed + Mother,
        data = Kohler.design,
        permutations = 999,
        by = "margin")

anova(dispersion)
```

```{r}
# 2. Run NMDS
# set.seed() is crucial for reproducibility since NMDS is non-deterministic
set.seed(42) 

# k=2 specifies 2 dimensions (NMDS1 and NMDS2) for plotting.
# trymax=100 is the max number of random starts.
ord <- vegan::metaMDS(dist_matrix, k = 2, trymax = 100, autotransform = FALSE) 

# 3. Check Stress (Lower is better; typically < 0.2 is acceptable)
cat("\nNMDS Stress:", round(ord$stress, 3), "\n")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

# 4. Extract NMDS site (sample) scores
ord_df <- data.frame(ord$points) %>%
  # Make the SampleID (rownames) an actual column
  rownames_to_column(var = "SampleID") %>%
  # Rename columns for clarity
  dplyr::rename(NMDS1 = MDS1, NMDS2 = MDS2)

# 5. Extract and prepare metadata
# Kohler.design should already be a data frame from previous steps,
# but ensure SampleID is a column for merging.
Kohler.design$SampleID <- rownames(Kohler.design)

# 6. Merge NMDS scores with metadata
# 'ord_data' is the final data frame for ggplot
ord_data <- dplyr::left_join(ord_df, Kohler.design, by = "SampleID")
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# --- NMDS PLOT ---

# Prepare the PERMANOVA summary text for annotation
permanova_res <- data.frame(
  R2 = c(0.08724, 0.21093, 0.12051),
  P = c(0.003, 0.001, 0.001)
)
rownames(permanova_res) <- c("SampleType", "Age", "Feed")

permanova_text <- paste(
  "PERMANOVA (Bray-Curtis):",
  "\nNMDS Stress =", round(ord$stress, 3),
  "\nAge: R² = ", round(permanova_res["Age", "R2"], 3), ", P = ", permanova_res["Age", "P"], "***",
  "\nSample Type: R² = ", round(permanova_res["SampleType", "R2"], 3), ", P = ", permanova_res["SampleType", "P"], "**",
  sep = ""
)

# Plotting the NMDS
p_nmds <- ggplot(ord_data, aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2,
                              color = SampleType, shape = Feed)) +
    
    # 7. Add Ellipses for the most impactful factor (Age, but using SampleType for clearer legend)
    stat_ellipse(aes(group = SampleType), linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.6) +
    
    # 8. Add Points
    geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
    
    # 9. Facet by the strongest factor (Age)
    facet_wrap(~ Age) +
    
    # 10. Add Labels and Theme
    labs(title = "NMDS Ordination of Microbial Communities",
         x = "NMDS1", y = "NMDS2",
         color = "Sample Type", shape = "Feed Status") +
    
    # Add the PERMANOVA results as an annotation (placed in the top-left of the first facet)
    geom_text(x = -Inf, y = Inf,
              label = permanova_text, 
              hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.05, 
              size = 3.5, 
              data = data.frame(Age = factor(levels(ord_data$Age)[1])), # Ensures annotation is in the first facet
              inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "right",
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95"))

print(p_nmds)
#
```
